newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT - HK's ABC downgraded.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - HK's ABC downgraded.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said it downgraded ABC Communications (Holdings) Ltd to "underperform" from "buy" due to price pressure in Hong Kong's cellular market.
The current run in ABC's share price assumes a value for GSM cellular provider SmarTone Mobile Communications Ltd that may or may not be achieved, said a report from U.S. brokerage.
SmarTone, 15 percent owned by ABC and 40 percent by Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd, is considering a Hong Kong listing.
For fiscal 1997, SmarTone should produce about 63 percent of ABC's pretax profit of ABC, with the Hong Kong paging business providing 34 percent, Salomon said.

The report said estimating SmarTone's value was extremely sensitive to how quickly average revenue per subscriber drops, and a steady erosion was expected as cellular becomes more of a commodity business in Hong Kong, it said.

"Since several equally reasonable estimates of price pressure in the Hong Kong cellular market produce drastically different prices for SmarTone, the best way to win this guessing game is to not play," the report said.
"Our analysis indicates that investors should take advantage of the current liquidity in ABC's shares to cash out," it said.
ABC shares were up HK$0.025 to HK$2.575 at midday.
